findings.description: After the revert, the skill still asks for prior_importants as {file, line, description, status} and never says how to number entries, while the schema and poster now require {from, index, status} with index counting every element; a model that counts only owed entries makes the poster and metrics resolve the wrong carried important.
findings.body:
**Concern.** Commit ff6fef8 reverts 15470cf. At head, the skill still tells the model to copy each prior important:

> `prior_importants`: ... each `{file, line, description, status}` (`description` copied from the prior record ...). Copy every still-unresolved entry forward

After this merges, `print-schema` (and so `--json-schema`) requires `{from, index, status}`. Only the schema's description explains how to count: "counting every element from 0, whatever its tag or status" ([review-metrics.schemas.ts#L64-L73](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ff6fef8d45d4c421e260ffdce3eebc7464d40e19/tools/review/src/review-metrics.schemas.ts#L64-L73)). The skill is the model's main instruction, and it only talks about "its `important` findings" and "the `unresolved` entries of its own `prior_importants`" (§3, [line 62](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ff6fef8d45d4c421e260ffdce3eebc7464d40e19/.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md#L62)). That invites counting only the owed entries. The docs and context reviewers raised the same contradiction.

**Trigger.** Records written by the new metrics step keep resolved entries in `prior_importants`, because `priorImportants` returns entries of both statuses. Take `prior_importants: [X resolved, Y unresolved, Z unresolved]`, where Z is fixed and Y is still open. A model that counts only owed entries sends:
- `{prior_importants, 0, unresolved}` for Y. Index 0 is X, which nothing owes, so the verdict is ignored.
- `{prior_importants, 1, resolved}` for Z. Index 1 is Y, so Y is marked resolved and dropped.

The review body and the next round's record now carry the fixed Z and lose the open Y.

**Fix.** Re-apply 15470cf so the skill and the schema agree. Line 62 should also say the model records a `{from, index, status}` verdict ([SKILL.md#L179](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ff6fef8d45d4c421e260ffdce3eebc7464d40e19/.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md#L179-L179)).
findings.suggestion: - `prior_importants`: when the Mode line names a prior record, one verdict per `important` entry of its `findings` and per `unresolved` entry of its own `prior_importants`, each `{from, index, status}`: `from` is the array (`findings` or `prior_importants`), `index` the entry's position in it counting every element from 0 whatever its tag or status, and `status` `resolved` or `unresolved` against the current head (§3). Copy nothing else from the record: the poster names each entry from the record itself, so its bullet is the text its thread was posted with, and it carries forward every entry you do not mark `resolved`, round after round. Empty only when the Mode line names no prior record.

findings.description: priorImportants promises that a misnumbered verdict keeps the important open, but a verdict counted off by the non-owed elements lands on another owed entry and resolves it, dropping a still-open important from the poster's body and the stored record.
findings.body:
**Concern.** The docstring says "a verdict the model left out or misnumbered keeps the important open rather than dropping it". That is only true when the wrong index points at a non-owed element or past the end of the array. Those are the only two cases the test covers (`findings` index 0, which is a nit, and `prior_importants` index 9). The lookup never checks that the model numbered the arrays the way the code does:

```ts
const said = verdicts.filter((verdict) => verdict.from === from && verdict.index === index);
const resolved = said.length > 0 && said.every((verdict) => verdict.status === "resolved");
```

**Trigger.** Take a record with `prior_importants: [X resolved, Y unresolved, Z unresolved]` (the metrics step at `review-metrics.script.ts:286` stores both statuses), or `findings: [nit, A, B]`, and a model that counts only owed entries. With Y still open and Z fixed, the verdict `{prior_importants, 1, resolved}` meant for Z resolves Y instead. The poster (`post-review.script.ts:206`) and the metrics record (`review-metrics.script.ts:286`) both go through this function, so Y disappears from the body and from every later round. This fails open, not closed, and it stays possible after the skill text is fixed.

**Fix.** A model that counts only owed entries always lands its first wrong index on an element nothing owes. So a verdict that points at a non-owed entry means the numbering can't be trusted, and ignoring all verdicts keeps every entry open (fail-closed). The existing tests still pass with this change. A test for the off-by-owed case would pin it ([permalink](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ff6fef8d45d4c421e260ffdce3eebc7464d40e19/tools/review/src/prior-record.utils.ts#L29-L62)).

findings.description: The call-site comments here and at review-metrics.script.ts:281-282 restate the prior-record.utils.ts module doc ("named from the prior record, never from the model's copy"); AGENTS.md §Comments says to delete a call-site copy of what the seam already says.

The REVIEW_PRIOR_RECORD env override is used only by its own unit test: no workflow or script sets it, and RUNNER_TEMP already lets tests pick the path. Dropping the `env.REVIEW_PRIOR_RECORD ??` branch removes a knob that maintainers would otherwise treat as a supported contract.
